subject.title: [voice-call] OpenAI realtime: audio clipping / breaking inside words during first ~30s of outbound calls (Twilio mulaw output)

question: Should Voice Call first require live Twilio/OpenAI output evidence before changing default OpenAI realtime telephony audio behavior, or should maintainers sponsor a conservative default change such as attenuation or extra diagnostics now?
rationale: The report is credible and user-facing, but current main already changed the default format path to audio/pcmu and the remaining fix choice could affect all realtime Voice Call audio without live proof of the failing layer.

options.title: Require live proof first
options.body: Collect redacted audio or logs showing levels, queueing, and provider/carrier frames before changing default output behavior.

options.title: Add diagnostics first
options.body: Sponsor a narrow instrumentation PR for peak levels, queue depth, underruns, and carrier frame timing without changing audio output yet.

options.title: Apply conservative attenuation
options.body: Intentionally add a default headroom change for OpenAI-to-telephony output and own the risk of altered loudness across realtime calls.

recommendation.title: Require live proof first
recommendation.body: Collect redacted audio or logs showing levels, queueing, and provider/carrier frames before changing default output behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The likely decision spans shared codec behavior, Voice Call runtime behavior, and maintainer-visible product risk, and steipete has recent history in the codec and Voice Call docs/runtime area.
